record.context_brief: convexity and max stability of DMA
record.original_question: For a compact Kahler manifold (X, omega), determine whether DMA(X, omega) is convex and whether, whenever phi belongs to DMA(X, omega) and psi belongs to PSH(X, omega), the function max(phi, psi) must also belong to DMA(X, omega).

evidence.quote: Question 6 (Coman-Guedj-Zeriahi). Is DMA(X, omega) convex ? If phi in DMA(X, omega) and psi in PSH(X, omega), does it imply that max(phi, psi) in DMA(X, omega) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, where $\omega$ is a smooth Kähler form. Denote by $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ the set of $\omega$-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$, i.e. upper semicontinuous functions $\varphi : X \to [-\infty,+\infty)$, $\varphi \not\equiv -\infty$, such that $\omega + dd^c\varphi \ge 0$ in the sense of currents. 

Define $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ to be the domain of definition of the complex Monge–Ampère operator on $(X,\omega)$, namely the set of all $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ for which there exists a (necessarily unique) Radon measure $\mathrm{MA}(\varphi)$ on $X$ with the following property: for every decreasing sequence $(\varphi_j) \subset \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega) \cap L^\infty(X)$ converging pointwise to $\varphi$, the measures $(\omega + dd^c\varphi_j)^n$ converge weakly to $\mathrm{MA}(\varphi)$, and the same limit is obtained for any such approximating sequence. (Equivalently, $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ is the largest subclass of $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$ on which the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère operator extends in a way that is continuous under decreasing sequences of bounded $\omega$-psh functions.)

Determine whether the following two statements are true:

(a) The set $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ is convex; that is, for every $\varphi_0, \varphi_1 \in \mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ and every $t \in [0,1]$, the function $(1-t)\varphi_0 + t\varphi_1$ belongs to $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$.

(b) Whenever $\varphi \in \mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ and $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega)$, the function $\max(\varphi,\psi)$ belongs to $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to Coman–Guedj–Zeriahi, concerns whether the domain of definition $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ of the Monge–Ampère operator on a compact Kähler manifold is convex and stable under taking maxima with arbitrary $\omega$-psh functions. The class $\mathrm{DMA}(X,\omega)$ was introduced and studied by Coman–Guedj–Zeriahi (2007). Searches did not surface a definitive resolution of either (a) or (b) in the published literature; the problem appears to remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: Domains of definition of Monge-Ampère operators on compact Kähler manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces and studies the class DMA(X,ω) of ω-psh functions for which the Monge-Ampère operator is well defined on a compact Kähler manifold.
status_evidence.claim: Defines DMA(X,ω) and studies its basic properties; convexity and max-stability are not established there in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Vincent Guedj, Ahmed Zeriahi: Degenerate Complex Monge-Ampère Equations (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the domain of definition DMA(X,ω) of the complex Monge-Ampère operator and notes open problems regarding its structure, including whether it is convex on certain manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The convexity of DMA(X,ω) is highlighted as an open/special problem.
